clue.text: Brand new university appointee’s mislaid cope

indicators.note: something mislaid has gone missing, so a letter is lost from the word it belonged to

blocks.note: a brand of car or radio is its make
a don is a university lecturer or fellow
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A freshly hired academic has lost his ecclesiastical cloak, the cope a priest wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand new' reads as one phrase but splits, with 'new' the letter that the academic mislays. 'Cope' looks like the vestment; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with whatever is available, which is exactly what coping means as a verb.

clue.text: Predator plunges medic upside down into Löwenbräu?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning letters upside down makes them read from bottom to top
one group of letters is put into the middle of another word

blocks.note: Löwenbräu is a German beer, and Bier is the German word for beer; the question mark flags the example
to plunge briefly is to dip
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A hunter dives headlong, dragging a doctor into a famous Munich lager.
explanation.walkthrough: The beer must be put into German, since Löwenbräu is a German brand. In a down clue, upside down means the letters read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird-spider is a large tarantula said to catch small birds, so it is a predator.

clue.text: Prepares for engagement feast and stocks reserves

indicators.note: to reserve is to keep something held back inside, so the letters are held within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready for a wedding lays on a banquet and fills up the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' suggests a betrothal and 'reserves' suggests stockpiling; the first is a battle and the second just holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In military usage, troops stand to when they take up positions ready to repel an attack, preparing for battle.

clue.text: Too dry to wear something up top

indicators.note: whoever wears a garment is inside it, so these letters go inside the item worn

blocks.note: a hat is something worn on top of the head
TT means teetotal, someone who stays dry

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is far too dry to put on your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' looks like an intensifier for 'dry', but it stands alone as the definition. TT, for teetotal, is a crossword standard for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'at that' is used as an additive tag meaning also or besides, as in 'cheap, and good at that'.

clue.text: Carmen playing in top theatre is inspired? Mercury seen to rise in it?

definitions.text: Carmen playing in top theatre is inspired? Mercury seen to rise in it?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upwards
playing loosely puts letters into motion and a new order
what is inspired is breathed in, so these letters are drawn inside the outer pair

blocks.note: read as car men: the AA, the Automobile Association, whose patrolmen rescue broken-down cars
Hg is the chemical symbol for mercury
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Bizet's Carmen staged at a great opera house, and Freddie Mercury's rise to fame on a famous record.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition. 'Carmen' is the opera but splits as car men, the AA. A Night at the Opera is Queen's 1975 album, with Bohemian Rhapsody, on which singer Freddie Mercury rose to stardom.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing Carmen performed in a top theatre is literally an evening spent at an opera house, and the Queen album carries this exact title.

clue.text: See 4
One man’s name and number being ill-directed?

definitions.text: One man’s name and number being ill-directed?

blocks.note: split as mis-taken: taken in the wrong direction
ID, identification, is the name and number on a card or document
an entity is a being, a thing that exists

explanation.surface: A person's name and official number end up attached to the wrong individual.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads in order backwards: 'ill-directed' gives the first word, and 'name and number' plus 'being' build the second.
explanation.definitionFit: When one person's name and identifying number are wrongly applied to another person, that confusion is the classic plot device of misidentification.

clue.text: One leading Kurds from the south can unite

indicators.note: the one at the front of a group is its leader, so the opening letter is taken
in a down entry, reading from the south means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a tin is a can
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A leader from the Kurdish south is able to bring people together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb 'is able to', but it is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones knit when they join back together, and people knit together when they become united.

clue.text: We’re not for feeding easy answers from the floor

indicators.note: food being fed goes inside, so the letters sit within the phrase
in a down entry, starting from the floor means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Someone in a debate objects to handing out simple replies to questions from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the floor' sounds like audience questions in a debate, and it also fits the definition, since votes are cast from the chamber floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The nays are those voting against a motion, so they can say of themselves that they are not in favour.

clue.text: I’ll take badgers a drink

blocks.note: taken as written
a cete is the collective noun for a group of badgers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone offers to carry a drink out to the badgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgers' looks like a verb, as in pestering someone, but it is the animals. Cete is an obscure collective noun for them, like a pride of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea, also written ice tea, is a cold beverage of sweetened chilled tea.

clue.text: See 6
Fish with it: rivers matter

blocks.note: to be hip is to be fashionable or with it
the Po in Italy and the Cam in Cambridge are two rivers
matter here is pus, as in a wound discharging matter

explanation.surface: An angler's tip: fish where the rivers count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' wants to mean 'be important'; here it is the noun for discharge from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocampus is the genus of seahorses, which are true bony fish despite the horse-like head.

clue.text: Forgetting conflict, rather wary about part of army set

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so some letters are dropped
one thing about another goes round it

blocks.note: a tad means slightly or rather, as in 'a tad cold'
the RE, the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
taken as written
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Putting a war behind it, a slightly nervous army unit is prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather wary' reads as one phrase but splits: 'rather' is A TAD, which goes about THE RE, and 'wary' forgetting WAR leaves Y. The definition, 'set', hides at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set means poised and prepared, just as a weapon held at the ready is prepared for immediate use.

clue.text: Weaver locked in cell since not entirely religious event of 1819

indicators.note: a word not given whole loses its tail end
something locked in is shut inside, so these letters go within the rest

blocks.note: peter is old slang for a prison cell
a loom is the machine that weaves cloth
as in 'as it was late', meaning since
sacred means religious; dropping its final letter leaves SACRE

explanation.surface: A weaver jailed because his faith was lukewarm, an incident from 1819.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: many of the Manchester protesters at Peterloo were handloom weavers. 'Weaver' wants a person; it is the machine.
explanation.definitionFit: In August 1819 cavalry charged a peaceful reform rally at St Peter's Field, Manchester, killing about fifteen people: a notorious historic incident.

clue.text: See 13
A near-Earth asteroid with the coordinates of comms facility

blocks.note: taken as written
433 Eros is a well-known asteroid whose orbit brings it close to Earth
to give an address is to say something is at a place

explanation.surface: An asteroid passing near Earth is located at the same position as a communications station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With the coordinates' just means located at, as in at 51 degrees north.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosat is an aeronautical satellite used for air traffic communications, so it is a piece of communications equipment.

clue.text: Coke woman’s snorting up features in Scottish tour

indicators.note: a drug snorted is drawn up inside the nose, so one word takes in another
in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom

blocks.note: a woman is she, and the apostrophe S makes it she's
Coke is the best-known cola

explanation.surface: A woman on a trip around Scotland is snorting cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coke' and 'snorting' point at the drug, but Coke is the fizzy drink, COLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lochs are long arms of the sea reaching inland along the Scottish west coast, typical scenery on a Highland tour.

clue.text: Code bearer carries refined poet’s words along parts of canal

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so these letters enclose the others

blocks.note: DNA carries the genetic code
U means upper-class, hence refined
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: A messenger with a cipher brings elegant verse along the towpath of a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canal' suggests a waterway; it is the alimentary canal, the gut. U for upper-class is a crossword standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The duodenum is the first section of the small intestine, which forms part of the alimentary tract; duodena is its plural.

clue.text: Birth to 2-year-old & 9+-year-old groups look to be excluded from these

definitions.text: Birth to 2-year-old & 9+-year-old groups look to be excluded from these

blocks.note: surface reading: a rule that leaves out the youngest and oldest children, as in a childcare scheme

blocks.clueFragment: look to be excluded from these
blocks.note: setter's reading: the enumeration (3-8) is itself the group that remains, so the words name the bands of ages that the excluded children fall outside

explanation.surface: A notice says babies and children of nine or older are not eligible for some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration is part of the clue: (3-8) reads as ages three to eight, exactly what is left when birth to two and nine-plus are excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names bands of ages used to sort people into categories, like those quoted in the clue.

clue.text: Virgin hunted down in reception

indicators.note: what is received is heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: to hunt down is to chase

explanation.surface: A maiden is pursued at a wedding party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' looks like a noun, but read as an adjective, as in virgin snow, it fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means never having had sexual relations, which is the adjectival sense of virgin.

clue.text: What’s at #20 – with missing humour – is ___

indicators.note: to go missing is to be absent, so the word that follows is struck out of another

blocks.note: the twentieth letter of the alphabet
taken as written
wit is humour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiz-style question asking what sits in a numbered slot once the jokes are stripped out.
explanation.walkthrough: '#20' looks like a pointer to this grid entry; it is the twentieth letter, T. The blank at the end is the definition: the answer completes the sentence 'What's at 20 is ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative word for the thing right here fills the blank, since the entry at 20 refers to itself.

clue.text: Left downtrodden, 20 writer does object to worship

indicators.note: trodden down puts it under foot, at the bottom of a down entry

blocks.note: 20 is THIS, and this writer is the setter, who calls himself I
taken as the singular verb do
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An oppressed author takes issue with religious devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object to' looks like 'oppose'; it is the noun object. 'This writer' is a crossword standard for the setter, so I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or person venerated as a god, literally a thing that is worshipped.

clue.text: Briefly horrible, honking smell at source?

definitions.text: Briefly horrible, honking smell at source?

blocks.note: surface reading: a disgusting, reeking stench traced to where it comes from
setter's reading: the gas's short form is its chemical formula, an H, a 2 and an S, which the first letters of the three words supply, being at source

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs out the origin of a short burst of foul stench.
explanation.walkthrough: Honking is British slang for smelly. The initials of horrible, honking smell are H, H and S, which written briefly is the formula H2S.
explanation.definitionFit: This toxic gas, formula H2S, gives rotten eggs their stink, so it is literally the source of a foul smell.

clue.text: Repair 75% of car light bulbs

indicators.note: three quarters keeps six of eight, so the last quarter is dropped
repairing means putting together again, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: the first six of the eight letters

explanation.surface: A mechanic's instruction to fix most of a vehicle's lamp bulbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulbs' sits beside 'light' to suggest lamps, but they are the plant kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic grows as an underground bulb of cloves, so heads of it are bulbs in the botanical sense.

clue.text: See 22
Understood terms have not been taken in

indicators.note: a term is an old word for a limit or boundary, so leaving the boundaries untaken drops the outer letters

blocks.note: fathomed means understood; without its first and last letters it shrinks

explanation.surface: Agreed conditions have still not been absorbed by those reading them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' looks like conditions of a deal; it is the archaic sense of boundaries, here the outer letters of FATHOMED. The definition is the last little word, 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in, rather than out, is staying indoors at their house, which is what at home means.
